title: Infra team playbook: GPU fleet, capacity, cloud accounts, IaC modules, CI/CD and runbooks
author: Alexandra Park
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates operational guidance, standards, and runbooks for Redwood's GPU fleet, capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking patterns, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD build pipelines. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and on-call responders. The document provides prescriptive steps for day-2 operations, capacity scaling, module interfaces, pipeline runbooks, and escalation paths.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce ambiguity for routine and emergency operations related to GPU capacity and infra automation; ensure consistent IaC patterns and safe rollouts.
- Scope: All projects that consume Redwood Dedicated GPU capacity or manage GPU-enabled infra, cloud accounts used for inference clusters (AWS/GCP), Terraform modules stored in infra-modules repo, and platform CI/CD pipelines that build and publish GPU images/services.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner_team: engineering (Infra & Platform).
- Document owner: Alexandra Park (infra-engineering lead).
- Oncall rotation: infra-oncall@redwood.com (see runbook for pager escalation).
- Tiered owners: GPU Fleet team (fleet-capacity@), Cloud Accounts team (cloud-ops@), Network team (networking@).

High-level architecture (summary):
- GPU edge service names: gpu-orchestrator, kvcache-proxy, inference-node, telemetry-agent.
- Provisioning flow: terraform -> cloud accounts -> iam + networking -> autoscaling groups/managed instance pools -> bootstrap (cloud-init) -> join fleet -> kube/node-provisioning -> node-labeling for model variants.
- Observability: Prometheus metrics (gpu_utilization, pod_token_latency), Grafana dashboards per model-route, and Datadog traces for orchestration path.

Capacity planning and fleet sizing methodology:
1) Inputs:
   - 99th percentile latency SLO per route (example: 150ms token latency for chat endpoints).
   - Expected QPS and peak concurrency for served models.
   - Model profile (tokens/sec, memory footprint, KV cache hit rate).
2) Unit sizing:
   - Define a unit GPU configuration (e.g., p4d equivalent, 8K context, quantized) and measure steady-state tokens/sec.
   - Example unit: p4d-like instance handling 80 streaming tokens/sec under typical prompts.
3) Buffer and redundancy:
   - Target capacity = (peak QPS * safety_factor) / (unit_throughput) where safety_factor = 1.4 for regular workloads, 1.8 for customer-SLA workloads.
   - Reserve 15% of fleet for emergency burst and scheduled upgrades.
4) Autoscale policy guidance:
   - Scale up triggers: sustained GPU_utilization > 68% for 2m, queue_length > 50 for 60s.
   - Scale down triggers: GPU_utilization < 28% for 5m and queue_length < 10.

GPU fleet operational thresholds (examples):
- Warning: avg GPU_utilization > 55% for 15m.
- Critical: avg GPU_utilization > 75% for 5m -> trigger paging.
- Node OOM rate > 0.5% within 1h -> investigate model memory regressions.

Cloud accounts and networking patterns:
- One cloud account per region per environment (prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-west-1, staging-us-west-2).
- Accounts must be onboarded via cloud-accounts repo with these minimum artifacts:
  1. Account bootstrap terraform: organization-level policies, SCPs (AWS), GCP org policies.
  2. Networking baseline: VPC CIDR, subnets (public/private), NAT gateways, route tables, transit gateway or VPC peering, and egress filter list.
  3. IAM roles + trust boundaries for bootstrap and platform controllers.
- Networking guidelines:
  - Use transit gateway for cross-AZ/region model fallback traffic.
  - Private subnets for inference nodes with egress through central NAT or Egress Gateway that enforces egress filtering and telemetry.
  - Use prefix lists for partner IP ranges and maintain in infra-dns.

Terraform / IaC modules (conventions and example):
- Repo: infra-modules (mono-repo of reusable modules). Modules must include: README, examples/, inputs.tf (documented), outputs.tf, semantic_version in module root.
- Standard modules and responsibilities:
  - module/gpu_node_pool: manages instance/VM pool, autoscaling policies, instance profiles, and GPU driver bootstrap.
  - module/network_base: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT, gateway attachments.
  - module/account_bootstrap: org policies, cloud logging, monitoring sink.
  - module/iam_roles_platform: cross-account roles for controllers, SSM/KMS roles.
- Module interface examples (table represented as monospace in doc):
  - gpu_node_pool inputs: region, instance_type, desired_capacity, min_size, max_size, gpu_driver_version, autoscale_triggers.
  - gpu_node_pool outputs: node_pool_id, instance_profile_arn, node_security_group_id.

Example usage snippet (terraform):
```hcl
module "inference_gpu_pool" {
  source          = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//gpu_node_pool?ref=v1.3.0"
  region          = "us-west-2"
  instance_type   = "p4d.24xlarge"
  desired_capacity= 12
  min_size        = 6
  max_size        = 24
  gpu_driver_version = "525.85"
}
```

CI/CD and build pipeline standards:
- Pipeline repos: infra-ci, gpu-images, platform-deploy. Pipelines are implemented in GitHub Actions for infra modules and in Jenkins for heavy parallel GPU image builds.
- Branching and release rules:
  - module changes: feature branch -> PR with CHANGELOG update and terraform plan review -> merge to main triggers module release (semantic version tag).
  - Image builds: every merge to release branch triggers nightly image build and canary promotion to staging.
- Canonical pipeline stages for infra modules:
  1) lint (tflint, checkov), 2) unit tests (terragrunt unit mocks), 3) plan (workspace specific), 4) policy checks (opa/gatekeeper), 5) apply in non-prod (manual approval for prod apply).
- Example GitHub Actions job name: terraform-plan-infra-modules.

Build and image provenance:
- Images must be signed and have SBOM published to artifact registry. Tagging format: redwood/gpu-inference:<module>-<sha>-<date>. Example: redwood/gpu-inference:inference-edge-7f3a2b-20260202.

Runbooks and incident procedures (concise playbooks):
1) High GPU utilization pager (P1):
   - Pager triggers: critical threshold breached (avg GPU_utilization > 75% for 5m) or queue_length > 200.
   - Steps:
     a) Acknowledge pager and post to #infra-incidents channel with initial context.
     b) Check fleet health dashboard: fleet-count, avg_util, node_unhealthy_count, queue_length.
     c) Evaluate fast mitigations: increase desired_capacity by +10% (if autoscale can't catch up) using terraform apply in the staging workspace or via autoscale override API.
     d) If provision lag > 3m, perform emergency redirect: modify routing policy in gpu-orchestrator to fallback model-variant with lower memory footprint (see fallback-policy playbook).
     e) If OOMs observed, cordon affected nodes and investigate model payloads.
     f) Postmortem owners: GPU Fleet team + SRE.
2) Node provisioning failures at scale:
   - Detect: node fails to join Kubernetes or bootstrap error in cloud-init.
   - Steps:
     1) Inspect cloud-init logs via SSM or instance console.
     2) If driver install fails, roll driver version to last-known-good and redeploy node pool.
     3) If more than 5% of nodes fail in a deployment, rollback via infra-ci pipeline and open urgent RFC.

Change rollout and migration guidelines:
- Canary sizing: 5% of traffic for 24h, monitor request success rate and latency regressions (alert if error rate delta > 1% or p95 latency delta > 12%).
- Large capacity changes (>= 20% fleet delta) require: preflight plan, dry-run apply in non-prod, canary in a single region, and scheduled maintenance window with stakeholders notified 48h prior.

Operational metrics, dashboards, and SLOs:
- Primary SLOs for infra team:
  - Node provisioning time: median <= 4m, p95 <= 12m.
  - Fleet availability: 99.95% monthly for production GPUs.
  - Autoscale correctness: scale action within 90s of trigger 85% of the time.
- Dashboards to maintain:
  - GPU Fleet Overview: total_nodes, healthy_nodes, avg_gpu_util, queued_requests.
  - Network: VPC throughput, NAT gateway errors, cross-region latency.
  - CI/CD: average plan duration, apply failure rate, module release cadence.

Maintenance windows and scheduled work:
- Weekly maintenance windows are Tuesday 02:00-03:00 UTC for non-production infra.
- Production maintenance requires 72h notice and coordination with customer success for any customers on Dedicated or Private plans.

Runbook examples (quick commands):
- Check GPU node pool size (aws cli example):
  aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names inference-gpu-pool-usw2
- Get instance system logs via SSM:
  aws ssm get-console-output --instance-id i-0abcd1234efgh5678 --region us-west-2
- Force scale via terraform (run in infra-ci workspace):
  cd infra/modules/gpu_node_pool && terragrunt plan && terragrunt apply -auto-approve -target=module.inference_gpu_pool

Post-incident review and regression triage:
- Every P1 incident triggers a postmortem within 72h with the following sections: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, remediation actions, and owner for each action.
- Regression triage: tie regressions to model eval sets and create a regression ticket in the model-onboarding queue if model change caused the issue.

Security, secrets and key management:
- KMS keys for instances are provisioned via account_bootstrap module. Customer keys (Private deployments) are managed in customer KMS with access controls.
- Never commit secrets to terraform code. Use SSM Parameter Store (encrypted) or Secrets Manager and reference via data sources at runtime.

Appendix: quick reference table (text):
- Default autoscale triggers: scale_up: gpu_util>68% (2m), queue>50(60s); scale_down: gpu_util<28%(5m) and queue<10.
- Default node labels: purpose=inference, gpu_type=p4d, zone=<az>.
- Image tagging policy: <service>-<sha>-<date>.
